findings.issue: decline_answer's docstring says 'The drive goes on to any task still open - the remedy a human added', and db2 pins that by calling decline_answer directly. Through `next`, a human who adds the remedy task first and then answers `--answer decline --reason <words>` is now refused at drive_locked:9408, because the decision is set aside while the remedy is ready. findings.issue: This is a user-visible change to a shipped verb, and neither the changelog nor the compatibility record mentions it. `audit-task.py scope <id> --gate Y` on a task whose tests.gate holds entries Y leaves out used to exit 0 and replace the list. It now exits 2 and writes nothing (`_scope_gate_refusal`, audit-task.py:10207-10244). New behaviour: `--gate-add`, the success-line clause 'tests.gate now holds [...]', and the `gateNowHolds` key in --json. COMPATIBILITY.md's contract covers the manifest and the config only, and `--gate` is still read, so no promise is broken. But the document records every earlier exit-code move on an audit-task verb 'because an exit code moved from 0 to 2 on a shipped command, and a pipeline that read ... is a pipeline that now stops' (COMPATIBILITY.md:546-556). The repo's precedent P153-R3 filed the missing CHANGELOG line for a `--gate*` behaviour change as a finding. No caller inside the repo is broken: commands, agents, skills, the drive (drive-phase.py only builds `scope --files` argvs, :3203 and :6817), tools, examples and .github build no `scope --gate` argv, and the suite's own replace-meaning callers (sn4, gc3, jf, fg1, fg3, dg4b, gx1) now pass --replace.
findings.resolution: Scope CHANGELOG.md and COMPATIBILITY.md into the task. Add an [Unreleased] '### Changed' entry: `scope --gate` refuses a list that leaves out a held entry unless --replace (exit 2, nothing written). Add an '### Added' entry for `--gate-add` and `gateNowHolds`. Add a COMPATIBILITY.md not-promised bullet, in the shape of the existing 'which FLAGS a verb accepts ... and it changed' entry, naming the exit-code move and the repair (`--replace`, or `--gate-add`).

findings.issue: The validator's wide-gate warning fires when a task's tests.gate is its phase's testGate verbatim. It tells the operator to 'Narrow it to the paths this task names ... go through `/audit:task scope <id> --gate "<command>"`'. A narrowed list leaves out held entries by definition, so after this diff that exact call is refused without --replace. This file is outside the diff, but the diff changed the verb on the other side of that instruction. The executor disclosed this, and the plan gate refused the edit. The refusal names --replace, so the cost is one round trip.
findings.resolution: Scope _manifest_phases.py, and tests/test__manifest_phases.py if a case pins the text, into this task or a follow-up. Say that narrowing takes `--gate "<command>" --replace`, while declaring the wide gate as the answer (the same list, which drops nothing) still takes a bare `--gate`.

findings.issue: `--gate-add Y` on a task that declares no gate of its own writes `[Y]` with gateBasis `declared`. Such a task has tests.gate absent, `[]` or all-blank, gateBasis not `cleared`, and `_mio.gate_entries` (_manifest_io.py:663-692) measures it by the phase's testGate. So the gate that grades the task silently shrinks from the phase's entries to `[Y]`. Yet the help text, task.md and verbs-in-full describe --gate-add as appending 'keeping every entry the task holds'. `_held_gate` and `_gate_added` read only the stored list, never the resolved one. This is the class this task closes: a call spelled as 'keep' loses entries the gate ran. The success line prints `[Y]` but not what it replaced.
findings.resolution: In `_locked_scope`, when `_held_gate(node)` is empty and `_mio.gate_entries(phase, node)` returns source 'phase' with entries, do one of two things. Either refuse `--gate-add`, naming the phase gate it would replace and the spelling that keeps it (`--gate <each phase entry> --gate Y`), or seed the append with those resolved entries. Add a gk case on such a task that tells the two outcomes apart.

findings.issue: The commit's count of 'declared' got wider, but what it stages did not. owned_rels now counts every fileIndex row keyed to the committing task. stage_targets still stages only task.files (commit-task-work.py:355-376). So a changed path that only a fileIndex row of the task names lands in undeclared_changes' `covered` (_scoped_commit.py:1507-1514). The commit treats it as work in flight: it does not refuse it and does not stage it. The file stays dirty and the task closes `done` without it. Before this diff the commit refused that path by name; now it drops it in silence, the outcome attempt_refusal's own docstring says it exists to prevent. The validator allows such rows: _manifest_crossrefs._check_file_index only requires files to be a subset of fileIndex, not the reverse. dp1 asserts the commit 'counts' src/indexed.py but never asserts the path is committed. Found by reading, not by a run.
findings.resolution: Treat `files` alone as declared. fileIndex is derived from files (`audit-task.py reindex`), so a row present only in fileIndex is drift: declared_task_map should not read fileIndex rows that no counted task's files covers. The hook then denies more, never less. Update dp1's expected list (src/indexed.py is neither opened nor counted). If fileIndex rows must stay, stage_targets has to stage every declared_task_map entry of the committing task. Either way, add a case: a path only the committing task's fileIndex row names is committed or refused, never left dirty after `done`.

findings.issue: redo_pin_spent counts a blocked task as spent even when its patch still stands. Blocked is not terminal: `unblock` returns the task to pending.
